result.title: Investment Consulting Services
result.summary: The City of Madison Police Officers’ & Firefighters’ Retirement System is a governmental defined benefit plan with $7.07 million in assets and 21 active members. Its five-member Board comprises one elected police officer, one elected firefighter, two City-appointed residents, and one member selected by the other four; it is subject to Public Records and Sunshine Laws. The Board seeks proposals from investment consulting firms for general advice and counsel on the Plan’s trust funds. Proposals must reach the City Clerk, 321 SW Rutledge Street, Madison, FL 32340, by 2:00 p.m. on September 1, 2025; late submissions will be returned unopened, and proposers must ensure the Clerk’s staff marks receipt by the deadline. Submit one original and five copies in a sealed package addressed to Lee Anne Hall, City Clerk, and marked “RFP No. 2025-0901 – Investment Consulting Services.” The advertisement also describes the procurement as Investment Consulting & Management Services.

result.title: PROPOSAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS
result.summary: The section solicits full-service investment consulting proposals for the Madison Police Officers’ & Firefighters’ Retirement System, specifying the submission deadline, delivery address, sealed-envelope labeling, and required original plus five copies. Proposers bear preparation costs, must submit clarification questions on time, monitor addenda, and report ambiguities. It describes the Board’s discretion to select, reject, waive, negotiate, cancel or re-advertise, and invite up to three firms to present; proposal withdrawal and validity periods; approval and execution requirements; Florida law and venue; public-records rules; and public-entity-crime, cone-of-silence, conflict, and non-collusion requirements. It also addresses disclaimers, requests for information, ownership and use of submissions, and termination for cause or convenience. Contractors must maintain required Florida-authorized insurance, including specified general and professional liability limits, additional-insured and primary/non-contributory terms, claims-made extended reporting, waivers of subrogation, certificates, and prompt notice of policy changes. Certain investment-manager communications must carry Florida’s prescribed disclaimer.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.summary: The City of Madison Police Officers’ & Firefighters’ Retirement System Board seeks full-service investment consulting firms to advise and counsel the Plan and support portfolio implementation; consultants report to the Board. Proposals must meet the stated conditions or may be rejected, and must arrive by 2:00 p.m. on September 1, 2025, at the City Clerk, 321 SE Rutledge Street, Madison, FL 32340. Submit proposals in sealed envelopes marked “RFP No. 2025-0901 – Investment Consulting Services,” with the proposer’s return address. Once opened, proposals become City and Board property and will not be returned.

nodes.title: 1-3 Number of Copies: Proposers shall submit an original and five (5) copies.
nodes.summary: Proposers must submit an original and five copies, bear all preparation costs, and submit written clarification questions by five days before the deadline. The Board may issue addenda until two days beforehand; proposers must check for them and report ambiguities in writing. The Board may select the most advantageous proposal, reject or waive requirements, negotiate, cancel or re-advertise; up to three firms may present on October 9, 2025. Proposals may be withdrawn within five days, then remain offers for six months; no binding agreement exists until approval and execution. Contracts incorporate the RFP, are governed by Florida law, and venue is Madison County. Proposals are public records unless statutory exemptions are properly identified. The text also establishes public-entity-crime exclusions, cone-of-silence limits, conflict disclosures, and non-collusion certification. The Board disclaims liability and warranties, may request further information, and may use proposal ideas. Submitted materials become Board property. Contracts may be terminated for specified failures or breaches after notice and opportunity to cure.

nodes.title: 1-18 Termination for Convenience:
nodes.summary: The Board may terminate all or part of the work when in the Plan’s best interest by notice specifying scope and effective date. The contractor must stop terminated work, complete unaffected work, and continue legal obligations until termination is final, regardless of payment adjustments. The provider must maintain, at its expense, Florida-authorized insurance throughout the contract, provide certificates/policies, and notify the Plan Administrator within 24 hours or the next business day of cancellation, nonrenewal, or modification; failure is a breach. The Board may require additional coverage. Required coverage includes occurrence-based general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence/$2 million aggregate, with the Plan as additional insured and coverage primary/non-contributory; and professional liability of at least $10 million per occurrence. Claims-made coverage must have an adequate retroactive date and, in specified policy-change or cancellation circumstances, a three-year extended reporting period. Policies must waive subrogation and recovery rights against the Board and related parties; provide no insurer recourse against the Board; and a current insurance certificate must accompany the proposal. Under Florida Statute 215.855, specified investment-manager communications discussing social, political, or ideological interests, subordinating shareholders’ interests, or advocating another entity’s interests must conspicuously include the prescribed Florida-views disclaimer.

result.title: NATURE OF SERVICES
key_items: 2-3 Scope of Services Requested: Services to be provided by the Proposer(s) shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
result.summary: The City of Madison seeks an investment consultant for its Police Officers’ and Firefighters’ Retirement System, established in 2019 and overseen by a five-member Board. As of September 2024, assets were about $7.07 million, the plan was 80% funded, and it served 15 pensioners with 21 active contributors. Mandatory qualifications include applicable business licenses, at least five years’ public-pension advisory experience, SEC investment-adviser registration, fiduciary status under Florida law, and acceptance of RFP terms; legal, accounting, and actuarial services are excluded. Requested work includes asset-allocation advice; manager and portfolio performance, risk, and benchmark reporting; custodian recommendations and coordination; policy, manager, and fund research and selection; monitoring, rebalancing subject to Board approval, regulatory updates, meetings, inquiries, fiduciary acknowledgement, education, and related periodic services. Proposals are evaluated for responsiveness, capability, experience, and fees. Submissions must describe the firm, staff, qualifications, independence and capacity; provide detailed fees, sample reports, litigation/regulatory and public-entity-crime disclosures, Florida-law knowledge, client totals, references, average client fund size, and at least five current public retirement-system clients.
